concept_options.title: What If AI Predicted Every Choice You Make?
concept_options.why_this_works: The topic title from the 2026-11-12 AI slate (g-ai-predicts-your-next-move, Gemini, 70/100 blind); the writer's pick; pairs with thumbnail a (TRUST HIM?)
concept_options.visual_approach: The food stall's counter at closing in a shuttered food court, one warm lamp over it (mood lamp): you large at the left, shocked, holding the cash-box key out across the counter on an open palm; the dark tin cash box between you; your best friend at the right, peach head, looking down at the key with a hand flat on the lid; over his head, on a thread from the city's small teal lamp, a crimson split-flap card reads 94%. The film's key shot (7:40). Three candidates a, b, c differ only in the tag (TRUST HIM?, HE WOULDN'T., IT'S WRONG.); drawn in code, brand/thumbs/predict
concept_options.hook: Closing time at a food court: your best friend holds out his hand for the cash-box key as he does every night, you pocket it as a joke, and a city worker clips a teal lamp to the lamppost; a tag drops over every head saying what each person will do in the next ten seconds, and the coffee next door goes half price for doing it.

selected_concept.rationale: The writer's recommendation (title A with tag a, TRUST HIM?); pending the owner's pick at G1

stages.approach: Packaging (G1, 2026-11-13): three titles, three one-variable thumbnails drawn in code (brand/thumbs/predict), the beat outline on the template spine with the owner's skit opening and played scenes; claims.md (31 rows) started at G1; the G1 room (story editor, claims check)

research, claims.md, script.md, sequel and 6-8 chapters on the template (rules/story.md #1-#19, 155 wpm, about 9.5 min); free local narration with each character in its own local voice, and a 720p first cut before G2; the G2 room; omni qc story_script must pass
Picture lock: cut, key shot, text, music by section with an ambience bed per set, and mix; the paid voice A/B only if the owner asks, at G3
The owner watches at 1x with cold viewers
publish.md and upload.yaml; private upload only when the owner asks

line_items.notes: Free and local. The paid voice only if the owner asks for the A/B, quoted first. G1 made no paid call: the thumbnails are drawn in code; the writer ran on the Claude subscription; the room used today's capped calls (story editor, claims check)

decisions.subject: Composition runtime

options_considered.label: The channel's paper-cut engine (core/engines/whatif)
options_considered.reason: The look the owner approved on 2026-11-06; figures timed to cue words; the set library is built for it, and the stall-counter thumbnail is drawn in it

options_considered.reason: Same library, but its stock scene types cannot draw the rig
options_considered.rejected_because: Would mean rebuilding the rig inside remotion-composer

options_considered.label: HyperFrames through video_compose
options_considered.reason: HTML and GSAP scenes; no rig, no cue timeline
options_considered.rejected_because: Would mean rewriting the approved look

decisions.reason: Proposed to the owner at G1 with the alternatives in one line each (packaging.md, Runtime)

decisions.subject: Setting

options_considered.label: Singapore, a food court and its train
options_considered.reason: The one real city that already bills a choice by road, traffic and time of day (c30), and aimed to put sensors on every lamppost (c30): the rule with one word changed

options_considered.label: An American city
options_considered.reason: The ledger's richest seam (c16, c17, c21, c22, c29)
options_considered.rejected_because: Each fact is a product or a courtroom with no picture over anyone's head; the film says them from the food court anyway

options_considered.label: An unnamed near-future city
options_considered.rejected_because: Loses the one real floor under a city that prices where you go

decisions.reason: The writer's call (packaging.md, Why this setting), kept by the session; plain words throughout (food court, iced coffee, the train)
